source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Sterling campus publishes 116 megawatts of IT capacity, the second-largest power budget declared by any data center in Virginia.

The campus covers three facilities, NVA5 through NVA7, with 1.18 million square feet of technical space. Virginia facilities that publish power figures total 1,603 megawatts across 25 sites, so this single campus accounts for 7.2 percent of the state's declared capacity. Capacity in Northern Virginia is not evenly spread. It clusters, and Sterling is one of the clusters.

For AI, the power budget is the number that matters, because accelerators are deployed against megawatts rather than floor area. At a typical training density of 40 kilowatts per rack, 116 megawatts could support roughly 2,900 racks. That figure is an arithmetic conversion, not a disclosure. The operator does not state what equipment is installed or how much of the capacity is in use, so 116 megawatts is a ceiling on the campus, not a measurement of it.

The published data also has a boundary worth naming. Of 330 data center facilities mapped in Virginia, only 25 have released power figures, which makes the 1,603 megawatt state total a floor rather than a census. For this campus specifically, the specifications list no certifications and disclose no total power draw, no PUE, no cooling technology, no grid interconnection details, and no constraints on expansion. Whether Sterling is currently limited by power supply or grid availability in Northern Virginia cannot be determined from what the operator has published.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
